detailed_rationale: [DATA] Uno Minda (auto components — switches, lighting, castings/alloy wheels, seating, acoustics, EV systems) reported FY26 consolidated revenue of Rs 19,589cr (+17% YoY) and normalised PAT of Rs 1,166cr (+24% YoY); Q4 FY26 revenue Rs 5,336cr (+18% YoY, +6.3% QoQ, record quarter) with PAT Rs 326cr (+22% YoY, +18% QoQ). Q4 FY26 revenue mix: Switches 25%, Lighting 22%, Castings 18%, Seating 7%, Green Mobility/EV 8%, Others 20% — a genuinely diversified content-per-vehicle book across 2W+4W+EV rather than a single-product story. Green mobility (EV systems) revenue Rs 1,405cr in FY26, +31% YoY off a still-small (~8%) base. Order-book adds skew toward higher kit value: sunroof cumulative order-book >Rs 3,500cr, an Android IVI/infotainment win at ~Rs 600cr annual peak value, a 2W lamps order at ~Rs 450cr annual value. Board has approved a ~Rs 550cr project for High-Voltage 4W EV Powertrain (DHT/EDU) capacity (1.85 lakh units/yr, SOP targeted Q2 FY28) and a plan to raise up to Rs 2,500cr via securities issuance to fund EV capex/subsidiary investments — this is a genuine capacity bet on the EV transition, not yet proven at scale, and carries near-term dilution risk for existing shareholders. [DATA] FY26 numbers per Business Standard/company release are net of 'prior period income and exceptional expenses relating to Labour Code' — flagged as the one-off to normalise for; reported PAT ex-exceptional is the Rs 1,166cr figure used above (treat headline PAT with care for one quarter of comparison). [DATA] Q1 FY27 results not yet out as of this review (2026-07-20); next scheduled results date per BSE filing is around 12-Aug-2026 — catalyst AHEAD, not behind. [DATA] Valuation: share price ~Rs 1,129-1,151 (early-mid July 2026), trailing PE ~67x — rich for an auto-ancillary, well above typical sector multiples (Samvardhana Motherson, Endurance Tech generally trade in the 25-40x band); consensus analyst target ~Rs 1,226 (modest ~8-9% upside from spot), bull case ~Rs 1,400-1,650 contingent on EV/kit-value story playing out, bear case ~Rs 920. Client base spans 2W (Bajaj, Hero MotoCorp, TVS) and 4W (Maruti Suzuki, Tata Motors, Hyundai, Honda) OEMs per company disclosures; granular customer-concentration % not disclosed in sources reviewed — flagged as an information gap, not confirmed as low-risk.

summary: Uno Minda closed FY26 with broad-based, volume-and-mix-led growth (revenue +17% to Rs 19,589cr, normalised PAT +24% to Rs 1,166cr) across a genuinely diversified 2W+4W+EV content-per-vehicle book (switches, lighting, castings, seating, sunroofs, EV systems), backed by real order wins (sunroof order-book >Rs 3,500cr, IVI win ~Rs 600cr/yr peak, 2W lamps ~Rs 450cr/yr) rather than one-off price effects; EV/green-mobility revenue is growing fast (+31% YoY) but still only ~8% of the base. The stock's trailing valuation (~67x PE) is rich versus auto-ancillary peers and prices in a high-execution EV/kit-value bull case, and a ~Rs 2,500cr securities issuance planned for EV capex introduces near-term dilution risk. Q1 FY27 results are not yet out (next filing expected ~mid-August 2026) — the near-term catalyst is ahead, not behind. No quant score exists yet in the internal pipeline; default Hold stands, with valuation richness as the primary watch item rather than a fundamental flag.
positive_para: [DATA] Genuinely diversified, mix-led growth: FY26 revenue +17% YoY, normalised PAT +24% YoY, Q4 FY26 revenue at a record Rs 5,336cr (+18% YoY) with margin improvement (PAT margin 6.59% vs 5.99% prior quarter, FY26 EBITDA margin 11.1%). Growth spans switches (25% of Q4 revenue), lighting (22%), castings (18%), seating (7%) and EV/green mobility (8%, +31% YoY) — not concentrated in a single product or OEM segment. Real, already-booked order wins support forward kit-value expansion: sunroof order-book >Rs 3,500cr cumulative, an Android IVI platform win at ~Rs 600cr annual peak value, a 2W lamps order at ~Rs 450cr annual value — these are wins, not just management commentary. Capacity is being built ahead of the EV curve (High-Voltage 4W EV Powertrain/DHT-EDU project, ~Rs 550cr, SOP Q2 FY28), positioning the company as an EV-transition-agnostic supplier (content grows whether 2W/4W goes EV or stays ICE, given the diversified product base) rather than a single-technology bet.
negative_para: [DATA]/[INFERENCE] Valuation is rich: trailing PE ~67x as of early-mid July 2026 is well above typical auto-ancillary peer multiples, leaving limited margin of safety if growth or margins disappoint even modestly — consensus target (~Rs 1,226) implies only ~8-9% upside from spot, meaning the stock is priced closer to the bull case than the base case. [DATA] A planned ~Rs 2,500cr securities issuance to fund EV capex/subsidiary investment is a real near-term dilution risk to existing shareholders, and the EV/green-mobility segment funding this capacity is still only ~8% of revenue — the payoff is multi-year, not immediate. [DATA] FY26 headline numbers are stated net of 'prior period income and exceptional expenses relating to Labour Code' per the company's own release — a one-off that should be normalised out before treating FY26 growth rates as clean run-rate. [DATA] Customer-concentration detail (exact % revenue from Bajaj/Maruti/Hyundai etc.) was not disclosed in the sources reviewed — company depends on 2W OEMs (Bajaj, Hero, TVS) and 4W OEMs (Maruti, Tata, Hyundai, Honda) whose own production cycles/monthly wholesale volumes remain the ultimate demand driver; this is a genuine information gap, not a confirmed low-risk read.
reverse_dcf_judgment: [INFERENCE] Rich. At ~67x trailing PE (~Rs 1,129-1,151 spot vs ~Rs 1,166cr FY26 normalised consolidated PAT), a simple 2-stage reverse-DCF (10yr explicit period tapering to a ~5-6% terminal growth, ~11-12% cost of equity typical for an Indian auto-ancillary) requires the market to be pricing roughly 22-25% sustained earnings/FCF CAGR for several years — meaningfully above even management's own FY27 PAT growth guidance band of 15-20% cited by covering analysts. The multiple is being paid for the EV-optionality + kit-value-expansion bull case (content-per-vehicle rising across switches/lighting/sunroof/EV powertrain), not the base case; a base-case ~15-18% earnings CAGR would suggest the stock is trading modestly to meaningfully rich of intrinsic support, consistent with the consensus target implying only single-digit upside from spot.
